hexa_cuda_build.what: Full hexa-lang -DHEXA_CUDA build linking runtime_cuda.c cuBLAS Dgemm body — NOT a standalone compile-test, an actual integrated hexa binary running on the GPU.
hexa_cuda_build.link_fix_landed: self/runtime.c — _hx_farr_table / _hx_farr_count were `static` (TU-local), so runtime_cuda.c's `extern` refs failed to link ('undefined reference to _hx_farr_count'). Fixed: non-static export under #ifdef HEXA_CUDA only; no-CUDA build byte-identical (still static).
hexa_cuda_build.build_gate_landed: self/main.hexa — cuda_build_cflags()/cuda_build_ldflags() gated by env HEXA_CUDA=1, wired into cmd_build native compile line: adds -DHEXA_CUDA -I<cuda>/include <self>/runtime_cuda.c -L<cuda>/lib64 -lcublas -lcudart. No-op (empty) unless HEXA_CUDA=1.
hexa_cuda_build.build_cmd: clang -O2 -D_GNU_SOURCE -DHEXA_CUDA -Wno-trigraphs -fbracket-depth=4096 -I self gpu_smoke.c self/runtime.c self/runtime_cuda.c -L/usr/local/cuda/lib64 -lcublas -lcudart -lm -lpthread -o gpu_smoke

f_rfc040_gpu_smoke.util_note: 2% peak — same reason as the bench: small matrices, cuBLAS finishes in microseconds vs the 200ms nvidia-smi sample period. Real-GPU proof is cuda_available()=1 (driver-probed), the exact 4.44e-15 cuBLAS-vs-CPU agreement (a stub returning the CPU result would show 0.0, not fp64-reduction-order drift of 4.44e-15 — the NONZERO-but-tiny delta IS the signature of real independent GPU reduction), and the bench's 51 TFLOP/s.
f_rfc040_gpu_smoke.tol_matmul_verdict: F-RFC040-GPU-EQUIV-RAND measured 4.44e-15 << proposed 1e-9 — comfortably within TOL_MATMUL for the smoke's shapes. (The committed result.json separately documents one reduction-heavy bench shape at 1.905e-9; the measurement-calibrated bound there is ~2e-9. The smoke's shapes stay 6 orders under 1e-9.)
